title: Hotel Booking Platform
description: A high-performance hotel discovery and booking experience with supplier integrations, flexible payments, and a modern search flow.

fields.context: A full-stack travel platform designed around fast hotel discovery, supplier inventory, and a frictionless checkout journey.
fields.problem: Travel inventory is fragmented, image-heavy, and latency-sensitive. Users need useful results quickly without sacrificing booking flexibility.
fields.solution: A server-rendered application combines provider APIs, caching, streamed search results, optimized media delivery, and a modular booking pipeline.

steps.title: Map the problem
steps.text: Travel inventory is fragmented, image-heavy, and latency-sensitive. Users need useful results quickly without sacrificing booking flexibility.

steps.title: Shape the experience
steps.text: A server-rendered application combines provider APIs, caching, streamed search results, optimized media delivery, and a modular booking pipeline.

steps.title: Connect the architecture
steps.text: Laravel powers the application and integrations while React and Inertia provide a rich interface. Redis is used for caching and queues, with a strong focus on resilient external API boundaries.

steps.title: Review the trade-offs
steps.text: The biggest challenge is balancing fresh provider inventory with response speed while keeping downstream supplier failures isolated from the customer experience.

outcomes.title: Designed outcome
outcomes.text: Designed as a scalable foundation where new suppliers, destinations, payment providers, and customer features can be added without rebuilding the core booking flow.

outcomes.title: Capabilities explored
outcomes.text: Supplier inventory aggregation. Streaming hotel search. Pay now / pay later checkout. Wallet and cashback flows. Optimized hotel imagery. Provider-aware booking orchestration.

outcomes.title: Evidence boundary
outcomes.text: This study expands an existing portfolio entry. No independent business metrics, client endorsement, or production deployment is asserted.

lessons: The biggest challenge is balancing fresh provider inventory with response speed while keeping downstream supplier failures isolated from the customer experience.
Keep the primary user journey clear as the product grows.
Treat operating states, exceptions, and future changes as part of the design.

title: A clearer view of the production floor
description: A manufacturing workflow concept for work orders, quality checkpoints, and traceable operational handoffs.

fields.context: An illustrative production team coordinates orders, quality reviews, and maintenance across separate records. This is a proposed system design, not a commissioned or deployed client project.
fields.problem: A status update can lose its meaning when the underlying event, responsible person, and next action are not recorded together. A single dashboard is not enough if the workflow behind it remains ambiguous.
fields.solution: Model each work order as an explicit sequence of operational events, with ownership, review checkpoints, and an exception queue. Show what needs attention before presenting aggregate charts.

steps.title: Map the handoffs
steps.text: Define the events that move an order forward and who can record each transition.

steps.title: Design a shared record
steps.text: Keep order status, checkpoints, and supporting notes in one traceable model.

steps.title: Make exceptions visible
steps.text: Separate blocked work and quality reviews from routine progress.

steps.title: Plan validation
steps.text: Evaluate representative scenarios with operational users before any production integration.

outcomes.title: Traceable status
outcomes.text: The proposed model links each status to a recorded event and responsible role.

outcomes.title: Reviewable quality checks
outcomes.text: Checkpoints become explicit workflow steps rather than informal notes.

outcomes.title: Planned validation
outcomes.text: No production savings, downtime reductions, or defect-rate improvements are claimed.

lessons: Agree on operational definitions before building a dashboard.
Exceptions need an owner, not only a warning color.
A concept needs user and integration validation before deployment.

title: A calmer home for everyday learning operations

fields.solution: Separate published course content from operational requests. Use clear role-based workspaces, accessible forms, and a reviewable publication workflow.

title: Make shipment exceptions easier to act on
description: A logistics operations concept for shipment events, exception ownership, and follow-up queues.

fields.context: A fictional dispatch operation receives updates from multiple sources. This portfolio scenario illustrates coordination problems without claiming a live logistics implementation.
fields.problem: A shipment status alone rarely explains whether an operator should act. Missing updates, conflicting events, and unowned exceptions can become difficult to distinguish.
fields.solution: Keep event history separate from the interpreted shipment state. Provide a prioritized exception queue with reasons, ownership, and the next expected action.

steps.title: Define event contracts
steps.text: Record source, event time, and meaning before combining updates.

steps.title: Model exceptions
steps.text: Distinguish missing information from a confirmed operational issue.

steps.title: Assign responsibility
steps.text: Make follow-up ownership visible in the queue.

steps.title: Test difficult sequences
steps.text: Use synthetic late, duplicate, and out-of-order events to evaluate the design.

outcomes.title: Traceable updates
outcomes.text: A proposed event model retains the context behind a status.

outcomes.title: Actionable exceptions
outcomes.text: The queue groups a reason, owner, and next step.

outcomes.title: No operational guarantees
outcomes.text: No delivery-time, cost, or shipment-volume outcomes are claimed.

lessons: Source timestamps and arrival timestamps answer different questions.
An exception should communicate why it needs attention.
A late event should not silently erase a more reliable state.
